title: Replace the cabin air filter behind a car's glove box
instruction: Replace the cabin air filter behind the glove box with the new one.
context: Replacing the cabin air filter is routine work for automotive service technicians and mechanics (about 0.7 million US workers), and on many cars the filter sits behind the glove box. The box only drops past its stops while both side walls are squeezed in at the same time; one side at a time does nothing, and forcing it breaks a stop.
setup: Station table (top 0.7475 m). Robot base frame: x forward, y to the robots' left. Dashboard mock-up, fixed, grey ABS, its opening facing the robots: front edge at x 0.32 m, centred on y 0; two side cheeks 12 mm thick, 200 mm deep and 400 mm tall (up to the top panel) with inner faces 366 mm apart, a back wall 400 mm tall and a top panel on it, so the space behind the glove box is reached only through the box's opening. Glove box, tan ABS, 0.55 kg, hinged along its bottom front edge 30 mm above the table at x 0.32: a door 350 mm wide, 210 mm tall and 10 mm thick with a handle, and behind it a bin 350 mm wide, 120 mm deep and 160 mm tall. The upper half of each side wall (80 mm tall) flexes up to 10 mm inward under a 3 N push and carries a stop lug, 10 x 10 mm and 6 mm proud of its outer face, 115 mm behind the hinge and 90 mm up; matching stops on the cheeks hold the box open at 45 degrees, where it starts, resting on them. Past the stops it swings down and hangs at 92 degrees. Cabin air filter housing: a slot 206 mm wide and 35 mm tall in the back wall, its face 190 mm behind the hinge, its floor 190 mm above the table, 104 mm deep. Old cabin air filter, loose, 40 g: a dirty grey-brown pleated element 200 mm wide, 100 mm deep and 25 mm thick (a half-length element of the kind two-piece housings use), seated 2 mm inside the slot, with a pull tab 40 mm wide, 20 mm long and 2.5 mm thick at mid-height on its outer end and a blue airflow mark on its left edge. New filter, the same in white, lying flat, centred at (0.36, 0.33), on a fixed grey stand 60 mm deep, 120 mm wide and 189 mm tall centred at (0.37, 0.33) (the filter's corners overhang it), beside the dash, its tab towards the robots and its airflow mark on the left. No other objects.
scoring: Measured once everything has come to rest. 0 if, at any moment, the box passed through its stops (between 46.5 and 54 degrees open) while either side wall was pushed in less than 4.5 mm: that forces a stop past its lug and breaks it. 0 if the old filter was drawn from its housing (its centre more than 5 mm from where it started), or any of the new filter went into the housing, before the box had passed its stops (opened more than 54 degrees); picking the new filter up beforehand is fine. 0 unless the box passed its stops at some point. Otherwise: 0 unless every part of the old filter, its tab included, is at least 10 mm in front of the housing's slot. 0.25 if it is. 0.5 if also the new filter is home: its centre within 5 mm of the seated position along the slot and 3 mm across and up, square to the slot and top side up within 3 degrees. 1.0 if also every fingertip is at least 8 cm from the new filter and the box, and both filters and the box moved under 1 mm (the box under 0.3 degrees) over the last 1 s.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Slide the old filter back into its housing and put the new one back on its stand; swing the box up, squeezing its sides to pass the stops, and let it rest open on them.
fidelity: Rigid bodies and joints in PhysX. Each flexible side wall is its upper half sliding inward on a spring (300 N/m, 10 mm of travel; 3 N, softer than a real box's 10 to 20 N), and each stop lug a rigid block; a forced stop is scored, not broken. The box's damper and the filter cover's clips are left out, and each filter is a rigid block with a pull tab; its 200 x 100 x 25 mm size and mass are estimates for a half-length element.
